body.content: The 13-point minimum triangle area problem in the unit square is related to Heilbronn-type problems. The key challenge is that symmetric grid placements (like 3x3 + 4 corners + center) create collinear triples that zero out the minimum area. Any viable construction must break all collinearities while maintaining uniform spacing. The 4-fold symmetric perturbation approach (corners fixed, edge midpoints perturbed inward, diagonal points adjusted) seems most promising. The critical question is: what perturbation parameter delta maximizes the minimum of two competing triangle area constraints?
body.why_keep_this: This analysis frames the optimization problem and identifies the key design tension between symmetry and collinearity avoidance.
